description: CKD Stages 3-5 population. Clinical context: CKD staging is based on eGFR — Stage 3 (eGFR 30-59), Stage 4 (eGFR 15-29), Stage 5 (eGFR <15). Anemia of CKD (target Hgb 10-12 g/dL) is managed with EPO agents. Hyperphosphatemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism (elevated PTH) are hallmark complications. Metformin is contraindicated when eGFR <30.
do_not_flag: Creatinine values 1.5-10.0 mg/dL — this is expected in CKD stages 3-5; not implausible
BUN values 21-100 mg/dL — uremia expected in advanced CKD
Potassium 5.1-7.0 mEq/L — hyperkalemia is a major CKD complication requiring management
Hemoglobin 7.0-11.4 g/dL — anemia of CKD; target Hgb on EPO is 10-12 g/dL
PTH 66-600 pg/mL — secondary hyperparathyroidism is near-universal in CKD stages 4-5
Phosphate 4.6-10.0 mg/dL — hyperphosphatemia expected in CKD; treated with phosphate binders
CO2/bicarbonate 14-21 mEq/L — metabolic acidosis is a hallmark of advanced CKD
Calcium 7.0-8.4 mg/dL — hypocalcemia in CKD due to impaired vitamin D activation
Both lisinopril AND furosemide in same patient — standard combination for CKD with hypertension and fluid overload
Epoetin alfa injection frequency (3x/week) — this is standard dosing for anemia of CKD
Mean creatinine of 1.5-6.0 mg/dL across the population — elevated creatinine is the defining laboratory finding of CKD; it is expected and correct, not a data quality issue
Absence of metformin in diabetic CKD patients — metformin is contraindicated in advanced CKD (eGFR <30 / creatinine >1.5); it has been intentionally excluded from this template

required_drug_classes.rationale: ACE inhibitors/ARBs are first-line in CKD to reduce proteinuria and slow progression. Expected in majority of CKD patients.

required_checks: VERIFY that mean creatinine across the population is above 1.5 mg/dL. A mean creatinine of 3.0+ mg/dL is expected and correct for CKD stages 3-5. Do NOT flag elevated creatinine as a problem — elevation IS the disease.
VERIFY that anemia-related labs (hemoglobin, hematocrit) appear in the population given 45% anemia prevalence. If no CBC results at all, flag HIGH.
VERIFY phosphate and/or PTH labs appear in the population. If absent entirely, flag MEDIUM.
